metadata.note: The Burlington and Missouri River Rail Road - two legally separate companies of the same name that ran their own trains: the Iowa company (Burlington - East Plattsmouth main line and branches, first operation 17 Jun 1857, leased to the CB&Q 31 Dec 1872) and the Burlington and Missouri River Rail Road Company in Nebraska (Plattsmouth - Lincoln - Kearney Junction main line and its leased lines, 1870 to 26 Jul 1880, when the CB&Q took possession). Each feature is one opening stage or branch, drawn only for the years the B&MR itself operated it; the CB&Q continuation of every line is in the CB&Q layers. Both companies share one company string and one colour (Rule 4): a passenger saw one railroad, the 'in Nebraska' suffix was a legal device for the land grant, and the two were under common Forbes/Perkins control - a judgement call recorded in the research report (UNRESOLVED 1); each feature's legal_company says which company it was. Every start and end date is a literal ICC Valuation date unless its note says otherwise. Boundary years follow the repo's split convention (west_shore_railroad.geojson, ulster_delaware_railroad.geojson): the B&MR feature ends in the year of the operator change and the CB&Q feature starts in that same year.

metadata.geometry_method: opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap degree tiles (maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror) plus, per corridor, OSM abandoned/historic ways and rail-trails and every OpenHistoricalMap railway way (fetch_gap). OSM carries no Burlington-and-Missouri spelling of old_railway_operator in Iowa or Nebraska (probe 2026-10-31: CB&Q 1,126 ways plus 'Chicago, Burlington, & Quincy', 'Chicago Burlington & Quincy', 'Burlington Northern Railroad'; no 'B&MR', 'B&M' or 'Burlington & Missouri River'), so the successor tags were used as the own-company match. Each feature's geometry_quality gives traced vs documented mileage, every waypoint's distance from the line, the mileage by OSM tagging and any straight-line leg.
metadata.mileage_checks: Combined figures where a single stage has no documented mileage: Lincoln - Harvard + Harvard - Kearney Junction traced together against ICC 1917's ~135 mi (Plattsmouth - Kearney 191.79 mi built, less Plattsmouth - Lincoln); Lincoln - Seward (via Milford) + Seward - Columbus traced together against the Lincoln and North Western's 73.4 mi (ICC 1917). See the report back for the sums.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [ANCHOR] single-year spans, each the only proven year of B&MR operation and NOT an ending or a start of service: Creston - Hopkins, Chariton - Leon and Villisca - Clarinda (1872, Iowa B&MR, CB&Q lessee from 31 Dec 1872); Bloomington - Indianola, Lester - Hardy, York - Aurora, Aurora - Central City and Seward - Columbus (1880, opened Jan-Jun 1880 or, for York - Aurora, 'soon after' 3 Nov 1879; CB&Q from 26 Jul 1880). PASSENGER EVIDENCE: the ICC dates prove operation, not passengers. In-era passenger confirmation exists for Burlington - Fairfield (1858 Dinsmore), Albia - Chariton (1868G), Red Oak - East Plattsmouth (1870G; first through passenger train 17 Jan 1870) and every Nebraska line open by 1875 (y = 1875). Red Oak - Hamburg has only a 1870 working-timetable listing. NO in-era passenger letter exists for Fairfield - Ottumwa, Ottumwa - Albia, Chariton - Afton, Afton - Red Oak, the three 1872 Iowa branches, or anything in Nebraska opened after 1875 (Seward - York, Brownville - Nemaha, all the Republican Valley and Lincoln and North Western lines); their spans rest on ICC opening dates. The Nebraska Railway leaseholds (Nebraska City - Seward, Nebraska City - Brownville) have y = 1875 letters one year BEFORE the B&MR lease and 1884G after it, but none inside 1876-1880. UNRESOLVED: Iowa start 1856 vs 1857 (Wikipedia and a Palimpsest extract vs ICC 1917 - 1857 drawn); Kearney Junction 3/15/18 Sep 1872; Omaha and South Western opening 29 Jan vs 1 Dec 1870; Aurora - Central City 1 Feb vs 4 Apr 1880; whether any Kansas mileage beyond Hardy was B&MR-operated before 26 Jul 1880. A Chronicling America search for 1872 Creston / Leon / Clarinda and 1878-80 Red Cloud / Columbus 'first passenger train' stories would firm up the ICC-only spans.
